one_line: OpenAI launches policy push, AI firms announce major acquisitions, and concerns rise over LLM security and trust.

themes.title: OpenAI plans post‑midterm policy
themes.text: OpenAI will start a policy and public‑relations campaign after the U.S. midterm elections. It will advocate mandatory safety safeguards, speed limits on advanced AI, and rebranding its data centers as AI compute campuses.

stories.headline: OpenAI to launch post‑midterm policy push, propose AI speed limits and rename data centers

themes.title: AI firms pursue strategic acquisitions
themes.text: Guidewire announced a $1.7 billion cash purchase of AI underwriting firm Hyperexponential, adding AI‑powered pricing tools. Deepgram bought Daily, keeping its open‑source Pipecat voice‑AI framework, and ServiceNow acquired Israeli startup Sweep to accelerate CRM migrations.

stories.headline: Guidewire to acquire Hyperexponential for $1.7 billion in cash
Deepgram acquires Daily, keeping open‑source Pipecat framework intact
ServiceNow acquires Israeli startup Sweep to speed CRM migrations

themes.title: LLM security and trust concerns
themes.text: OpenAI fixed a chain of vulnerabilities in ChatGPT’s HTML preview sandbox and paid a $5,000 bug bounty after the issue was reported. Separately, Kyle Kingsbury warned that large language models are eroding trust in software documentation and code.

stories.headline: OpenAI patches HTML preview exploit that let attackers hijack ChatGPT accounts
Kyle Kingsbury warns LLMs erode trust in software documentation

themes.title: DeepSeek unveils open‑source Super‑Agent
themes.text: DeepSeek released Super‑Agent, an open‑source research prototype that monitors GitHub repositories and developer chats, then proactively suggests fixes or opens pull requests. The code is available under an MIT license and is not production‑ready.

stories.headline: DeepSeek releases open‑source Super‑Agent, a proactive coding assistant prototype
